one_line_contribution: That cross-model agent-memory harm is signed in the writer-to-reader capability gap (downward transfer hurts, upward does not) rather than a symmetric identity mismatch, that the cure is reader-in-the-loop selection rather than reader authorship, and that coupling a GEPA-style optimizer to the memory bank absorbs the harm in net accuracy while the break-count asymmetry survives underneath.
closest_prior_work: Agent Memory Distillation (arXiv:2608.07169), as the proposal itself concedes: it already reports that teacher-to-student memory transfer yields inconsistent or degrading results and that quality depends on teacher-student compatibility. That is the phenomenon plus a compatibility term, i.e. most of the qualitative content of Prediction 1. Rosetta Memory (2606.07711) collides on the framing that utility depends on the write/read model pair. What is left after both is narrow: making compatibility ordinal and signed, the quality/utility rank inversion, and the selection-vs-authorship split. Run D is the single cell that separates this proposal from Rosetta/MemCollab, and it is exactly the cell the plan runs at one bank replicate and labels directional only, so the discriminating evidence for the paper's headline framing is the weakest evidence in the design.
strongest_objection: Prediction 1's direction asymmetry is confounded with reader identity, and no arm controls for it. The difference-in-differences compares (8B reading the 14B bank minus 8B reading its own) against (14B reading the 8B bank minus 14B reading its own): the two arms of the DiD use different readers, so the well-known fact that larger models are less perturbed by any injected prompt text - irrelevant, scrambled, or merely off-policy - predicts the same signed asymmetry with no writer-to-reader capability law at all. Run L cannot break the tie because both its policies sit at the same capability level, and the shuffled-provenance placebo only tests bookkeeping, not reader sensitivity. Add to this that runs D, E, H, I, J, K are single-replicate and self-declared directional only, while Predictions 1 (mirror cell), 4 and 5 all rest on them, in a setting where the track's own pilot saw 5-14 point re-scoring drift. Prediction 5 compounds this by treating a failure to reject (H vs I falling below a 4-5 point MDE) as positive evidence of masking - that is accepting the null, on an underpowered single-replicate contrast, for one of the four claims the proposal says are its remaining novelty. Prediction 4b is separately broken as stated: GEPA (run G) searches 12 candidates scored on reader rollouts while run J is one cold frontier instruction, so candidate count and validation-set exposure differ alongside selection, and 'same author, selection is the only difference' is not true of the arms as designed.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, all inside the stated envelope if the n=300 cross-family arm (L) is dropped, since the proposal already concedes L cannot exclude a small stylistic effect. (1) Add a per-reader perturbation calibration: inject token-matched degraded items (scrambled, topically-retrieved-but-wrong, or same-bank items with actions corrupted) into 8B and 14B, and report the provenance effect normalized by each reader's own sensitivity to injected junk; without this the signed-gap law and 'strong readers absorb bad advice' are observationally identical. (2) Promote run D to two bank replicates and enter it in the mixed-effects model as a primary contrast rather than reporting it as directional. (3) Rebuild J as best-of-12 frontier-proposed instructions selected by the frontier model or by a held-out non-reader judge, so G vs J varies only who did the selecting, not how many candidates existed. (4) State Prediction 5 as a pre-registered equivalence test (TOST with a named equivalence margin) rather than 'falls below the MDE', and pre-specify the break-count contrast with an interval, since break counts on the order of 3 vs 6 items cannot support a 2x ratio claim (Prediction 3) at any useful confidence.
missing_baseline: Reader-probe selection applied to the self-written bank, and a non-reader-selected frontier bank (items filtered by frontier or held-out-model probes at the same admission rate). As designed, run K vs run C shows only that filtering a bank at fixed injected tokens helps - the track's own prior finding that cutting injection from seven items to three removed the harm makes generic filtering the leading rival explanation for the entire Prediction 4a effect. Without a probe-selected self bank (does selection help even when provenance is already matched?) and a non-reader selector (is the benefit reader-specific or just selection-shaped?), the paper's central 'selection, not authorship' claim has no arm that isolates the reader's role in selection. Second omission: a token-matched neutral-filler condition against run A, so that any bank-vs-no-memory statement is not confounded with context length.
preprint_collision: Unusually good by the standards of this exercise: it names specific arXiv identifiers with dates, dispositions each one, distinguishes collision-on-phenomenon from collision-on-claim, admits AMD is more damaging than a previous read, and states a residual risk. I credit it. Two real weaknesses remain. First, it reports conclusions but no searches: no queries, no venues, no date cutoff, no statement of what was searched and found empty, so 'nothing in the retrieved literature tests any of the four' is unauditable. Second, the search is aimed entirely at the cross-model memory literature and not at the claim the proposal calls its own most novel - that a prompt optimizer masks component-level harm in a coupled optimizer-plus-memory stack. Component-attribution and ablation-hygiene work on DSPy/GEPA-style stacks is the natural place for that to have been scooped, and the check does not report looking there. On the collision that is admitted: AMD's compatibility term plus Rosetta's write/read-pair dependence already occupy the descriptive claim, so the novelty that survives is the sign of the effect - which rides on the single underpowered cell (run D) flagged above - plus the selection/authorship split, whose isolating arms are themselves confounded. The proposal's own residual-risk sentence (a self-written-bank ablation sitting in some cross-model memory appendix) names precisely the finding that would leave only the masking result standing.
